research_rationale:
Executive Order 11593 of May 13, 1971 (36 FR 8921), Protection and Enhancement of the Cultural Environment, sets a federal policy of leadership in preserving the historic and cultural environment (section 1), assigns federal agency heads duties to inventory and nominate eligible properties, protect them in the interim, record them before alteration, maintain them, submit procedures annually and cooperate with transferees (section 2), and assigns the Secretary of the Interior supporting duties (section 3). It is issued under the President's authority "in furtherance of the purposes and policies" of four statutes (NEPA, the National Historic Preservation Act of 1966, the Historic Sites Act of 1935 and the Antiquities Act of 1906), none of which is the order's sole source of authority; the order contains no sentence that makes it depend on a statute's continuation, and no held source shows any of those statutes repealed. The held original is an official Federal Register OCR text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11593.txt). It contains dates (July 1, 1973 for inventories; January 1, 1972 and annually thereafter for procedures) and one contingent phrase (interim caution until inventories are completed), but each is a deadline, schedule or stage within a continuing duty, not an expiry; under the 2026-10-28 ruling a deadline is not an end and no held source shows any agency duty completed or withdrawn. No held later instrument amends, revokes or supersedes the order: the lookup of held texts citing the number found Executive Orders 13006 (May 21, 1996) and 13022 (October 31, 1996), which recite it as policy to be followed ("in furtherance of and consistent with" it; "consistent with the policy stated in Executive Order 11593") and neither amends nor revokes it; agency notices and a 2026 rule (91 FR 8072) that list it among authorities followed; the 1989 OFR codification entry; and the Code note under 54 U.S.C. 300101 that prints the order unchanged. The three bounded searches were read for coverage: the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, through 2026-10-09) hit two places, the eCFR search (as of 2026-10-14) hit 78 regulation passages that cite the order, and the Federal Register disposition catalog search hit only the cross references from Executive Orders 13006 and 13022. No ending was found. The current basis for each clause is the held original read with those searches; the Code note is a context source that the checker cannot quote-verify, so it is not cited as the source.
